Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.

**Working with oh-my-claudecode.** oh-my-claudecode (OMC) is the user's main harness. It owns every keyword and workflow, including requirements interviews, plans, multi-day programs, and project knowledge. omc-pstack-fy is the engineering engine OMC hands code units to and adds to its final review, through this plugin's bridge hook. Inside OMC workflows, each code unit runs one of this skill's playbooks as a `omc-pstack-fy:poteto-agent` delegate. The ai-slop-cleaner step runs the **deslop** skill. The final code review adds the **interrogate** skill beside OMC's `code-reviewer`. Outside OMC workflows, omc-pstack-fy's playbooks run when the user types a `/omc-pstack-fy:` command. With OMC installed and enabled, a standing program goes to OMC's ultragoal, team, or ralph. Inside an explicit poteto-mode run, this skill's rules still win over OMC's CLAUDE.md block and hook output, and delegates stay `omc-pstack-fy:poteto-agent`, as Subagents says, never `executor`.
edits.why: The owner's choice: omc-pstack-fy is OMC-first. OMC is the main harness and keeps every keyword and workflow, and omc-pstack-fy is the engineering engine inside it. The bridge that hands OMC's code units and deslop step to omc-pstack-fy and adds interrogate to its final review ships as the plugin's SessionStart hook (overlays/hooks/omc-bridge.mjs), which injects it only while OMC is installed and enabled, so nothing writes .claude/omc.jsonc, settings.local.json, OMC_SKIP_HOOKS, or a global rule file. OMC's CLAUDE.md block routes code to executor, so an explicit poteto-mode run still says its own rules win.

**Fable outside a panel.** Outside a panel, `fable` runs in three cases, and you say which. A role line or a skill's default names it, as `hardest tasks` does for the hardest changes. The user named it for this task. Two `opus xhigh` runs of the same brief failed its check.

**When Fable's quota runs out.** When a `fable` agent fails, at spawn or in its result, because Fable's usage limit or quota is reached, rerun the same brief on `opus` at the same effort and say so in the reply. This covers every `fable` entry. An arena runner seat and any other role that is not a reviewer reruns on `opus` even when that repeats a model, because arena allows repeated runner models. A reviewer panel (`interrogate reviewers`) drops the seat instead when `opus` would repeat another seat's model, and says that the panel ran one seat short, because a duplicate reviewer makes findings look independently confirmed. A pool that picks one entry moves to the next entry its own rule allows, because arena's judge never runs on the parent's model. A quota failure is not a rejected model, so the fallback order under **Match the model to the job** does not apply.
edits.why: The owner's choice of 2026-11-17. In the owner's words, the hardest tasks go to Fable, and when Fable's quota is used up, they go to Opus. Upstream v0.15.43 retired `hardest tasks` and runs Fable outside a panel only when the user names it or after two failed Opus xhigh runs. Those two routes stay, and a role line or skill default that names Fable is the third. The quota rule covers every `fable` entry, so one rule answers every spawn. Only a reviewer panel drops a seat that would repeat another seat's model, because a duplicate reviewer makes one model's finding look independently confirmed, as the pstack-ask fallback already says. Arena allows repeated runner models, so a runner seat reruns on `opus`. A pool that picks one entry moves to the next entry its own rule allows, because arena's judge never runs on the parent's model. It is a rule of its own, because a quota failure is not the Agent tool rejecting a model as not valid.
